messages.subject: reshape a spatio-temporal dataset
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to reshape a spatio-temporal dataset to a "long" format.
It's a 100 years' monthly rainfall data gauging in 78 stations. So the
original dataset is a 1200*78 matrix with date as rows and station IDs
as cols. What I want is to reshape it into a matrix with just three
columns(92600*3 matrix): IDs , dates and rainfall observations.
I have got it by three lines codes as following, which are very bumpy
and chubby.:
T<-t(matrix(rownames(rainfall),nrow=dim(rainfall)[2],ncol=dim(rainfall)
[1],byrow=TRUE))
ID<-matrix(colnames(rainfall),nrow=dim(rainfall)[1],ncol=dim(rainfall)
[2],byrow=TRUE)
obs_rainfall<-
data.frame(date=c(as.Date(T)),ID=c(ID),rainfall=c(as.matrix(rainfall)))
Could it be handled easily by any "reshape" functions?

messages.author: 294dd232bf4ab480
messages.subject: Re: reshape a spatio-temporal dataset
parts:
Hi -

Yes, the melt() function in the reshape2 package will do the trick.

library(reshape2)

## I think this what your data look like:
test <- data.frame(Time = 1:20, Sta1 = rnorm(20), Sta2 = rnorm(20), Sta3 = rnorm(20))

head(test)
  Time         Sta1        Sta2       Sta3
1    1 -0.849412015  1.11316981  0.9303466
2    2 -0.943124251  2.41267782  0.1310218
3    3 -1.134935071 -0.27169808 -0.7537679
4    4 -0.369759824  1.89524403  0.6356290
5    5  0.721777055  0.02020361 -0.4187980
6    6 -0.006843206 -0.63194414 -1.4004065

## check out ?melt for more info
testm <- melt(test, id.vars = 'Time')
head(testm)

   Time variable        value
1     1     Sta1 -0.849412015
2     2     Sta1 -0.943124251
3     3     Sta1 -1.134935071
4     4     Sta1 -0.369759824
5     5     Sta1  0.721777055
6     6     Sta1 -0.006843206
- Patrick
